newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ median house price reaches NZ$160,000 in Feb.
newsitem.headline: NZ median house price reaches NZ$160,000 in Feb.

text.p: The national median price for New Zealand houses sold in February rose 0.6 percent to NZ$160,000, compared to $159,000 in January, the Real Estate Institute (REINZ) said on Monday.
The median price was up 4.2 percent from the $153,500 recorded in February 1996.
"We have not previously seen the national median at this level," Institute president Colin Brown said.
"The residential real estate market is continuing to be very active and home buyers appear to be making the most of competitive interest rates currently available."

The Auckland median house price was $235,000, up 2.2 percent from $230,000 in January and up 6.8 percent from $220,000 in February 1996. A total of 2,803 sales were made in the Auckland region, a slight rise from January's 2,719 but down on 3,877 in February 1996.
"The Auckland market is continuing to remain buoyant with home sales and medians remaining healthy," Brown said.
The institute reported a national total of 8,033 sales by real estate agents in February, up from January's 7,815, but down from 10,024 in February last year.
Brown said although the number of sales was down on a year ago, the median price increased in all but three regions, keeping the total value of sales up.

"The steady increase in homes sold in most regions, combined with the increase in median prices across New Zealand, is an indication that buyers and vendors are taking advantage of the confident market," Brown said.
He said the figures also indicated that many buyers were seizing on real estate as an investment opportunity.
Northland experienced the largest median increase in the country, rising 14.5 percent, or $16,000, to $126,000 in the year to February.
Total home sales in Waitakere were down but sales rose in the other metropolitan Auckland areas.
Sales were steady in Waikato where 1,326 homes sold with a median of $142,000.
Manawatu and Taranaki were steady, while in Canterbury the total number of homes sold was up on last month and the median increased to $136,000, the highest in 12 months.
The median in Wellington of $145,000 was unchanged from January and the number of homes sold rose 49 to 912.
Otago also recorded an increased median of $108,000, with 300 homes sold.
Sales of sections of land also rose in February with a median price in February of $67,000, up $2,000 on the previous month. -- Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
